newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ABI EARNINGS HIT BY PRICE WAR WITH PEPSI.
newsitem.headline: ABI EARNINGS HIT BY PRICE WAR WITH PEPSI.

text.p: South Africa's Amalgamated Beverage Industries said on Wednesday that its half year profits had been hit by a price war with its rival Pepsi.
ABI, South Africa's largest Coca-Cola bottler, operates in the country's densely populated Gauteng region, which recently saw the entry of New Age Beverages, Pepsi's bottler.
ABI managing director Trent Odgers said the firm had been prepared for the clash with Pepsi and recaptured most of its market share in the province by matching its prices.
"The impact of this, plus high levels of marketing and container expenditure, eroded margins," he said.
Attributable earnings were up just one percent to 32.4 million rand and an extended capital base saw earnings per share dip two percent to 29.4 cents. The dividend was held at 11.5 cents a share.
The ABI figures are the latest sign of the hotting up of the so-called "Cola Wars" in South Africa as Pepsi seeks to expand into a national brand.
Pepsi also operates in KwaZulu-Natal and Durban-based Coke bottler Suncrush in September posted pre-tax profit for the year to June 30 edging down to 116 million rand from 118 million.
